overall_verdict: Under the brief's precedence and supplied-evidence rules, SAT-1 and SAT-2 are go, SAT-3 is hold pending a fresh TLE, SAT-4 is no_go for its below-minimum supplied link margin, and SAT-5 is no_go for its non-compliant disposal plan.
limitations: All data are synthetic teaching-scenario data for fictional NORAD IDs 99001-99005; these are not operational clearances.

All five link results used supplied_evidence with computed=false because receiver G/T or gain plus noise temperature, atmospheric_loss_db, data_rate_bps, and required_ebn0_db were missing; the atmospheric-loss retry was not triggered because each first call returned link_closes.

All four unblocked disposal responses had computed=false and required area-to-mass and passivation_planned; no estimated_lifetime_years or meets_25_year_rule value was returned, so disposal decisions rest on the declared post-mission lifetimes and the brief's rule rather than independent decay verification.

Each of the four accepted orbit results reported checksum_line1_ok=false and checksum_line2_ok=false despite returning computed ephemeris and elements; the optional standalone checksum pass was not run, so TLE integrity remains a caveat.
No absolute review timestamp was supplied to cross-check the declared epoch ages; the freshness outcomes therefore rely on epoch_age_hours exactly as provided.
Link closure and disposal compliance are assessments or predictions, not operational guarantees.
